Every field verified live against CourtListener on 2026-08-22 (search + opinions-cited endpoints), not recalled from training data. authorities.name: Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife
authorities.court: Supreme Court of the United States
authorities.proposition: The 'irreducible constitutional minimum' of Article III standing requires: (1) an injury in fact that is concrete, particularized, and actual or imminent; (2) a causal connection between the injury and the defendant's conduct (traceability); and (3) a likelihood that the injury will be redressed by a favourable decision (redressability). Established the modern three-part standing test.

authorities.name: TransUnion LLC v. Ramirez
authorities.court: Supreme Court of the United States
authorities.proposition: Applies Lujan's injury-in-fact requirement to statutory-damages claims under the Fair Credit Reporting Act: a plaintiff must demonstrate concrete injury even where a federal statute creates a private cause of action for a bare procedural violation - a plaintiff cannot rely on a statutory violation alone without a concrete, real-world harm (or a harm with a close historical/common-law analogue) to satisfy Article III.

edges.verified_via: CourtListener opinions-cited endpoint - citing_opinion 4698691 -> cited_opinion 9432577, depth 17 (strong, repeated reliance)

what_this_is_not: Two cases, one verified edge, on Article III's injury-in-fact/traceability/redressability test and its application to statutory-damages claims. Does not cover other standing doctrines (taxpayer standing, organizational standing, associational standing) not tested in this pass.
